FocusForce needs %1$d permissions to work. We will explain each one before Android asks, and you can skip any of them.
Everything runs on your device. Your usage data is never uploaded, and nothing on your screen is recorded or sent anywhere.
Skip (blocking will not work without this)
Lets FocusForce see how long each app is on screen, how often you open it and how often you unlock your phone. This powers your totals, charts, limits and the weekly villain.
We never see what you do inside apps. Usage numbers stay on this device and are never uploaded.
Lets your hero\'s full-screen block screen appear on top of an app you chose to block.
We only draw our own block screen, and only when you open a blocked app. We never draw over banking or other apps you did not choose.

FocusForce uses Android's Accessibility Service for one purpose: to notice which app or window has just come to the front, so it can show the block screen over apps you chose to block.

This version installs the service but does not yet act on any event. Features that come later, and only if you turn them on, add: detecting short-video sections inside apps, and reading the address of supported browsers to block websites on your list.

FocusForce never reads passwords, messages or anything you type. It never takes screenshots and never stores or sends screen content. Everything is processed on your device.

You can turn it off any time in Settings, Accessibility.
Detecting the app in front is the most reliable way to block on every Android version. Without it we fall back to polling Usage access, which is slower and less dependable on some phones.
We do not collect, log, store or transmit what is on your screen, and the service is not used for anything except the blocking features you enable.
Shows your focus-session timer, limit warnings and gentle break reminders. Android also requires a visible notification while the blocker is running.
No marketing and no spam. Notifications are only about your own focus and limits.
Many phones stop background apps to save power, which would switch your blocker off. Exempting FocusForce keeps it running.
This does not read anything and does not give us extra data. It only stops the system from pausing FocusForce. Some phones also need the extra steps listed under device tips.
Lets focus schedules start and end exactly on time, for example your Sleep profile at 10:00 pm.
Used only for the schedules you create. Nothing else is scheduled.
Live status. This page refreshes when you come back from Settings.
Some phone makers add extra battery managers that stop blockers. Menu names change between software versions, so treat these as a guide.

Open FocusForce app settings, then Permissions, and turn off the option that removes permissions or pauses app activity when the app is unused. Android can otherwise take back Usage access and Accessibility after a few months.

string-array.name: oem_tips_xiaomi
string-array.item: Settings, Apps, Manage apps, FocusForce: turn on Autostart.
On the same page set Battery saver to No restrictions.
Under Other permissions, allow Display pop-up windows and Display pop-up windows while running in the background.
Open Recent apps, long-press the FocusForce card and choose Lock so it is not cleared.

string-array.name: oem_tips_oppo
string-array.item: Settings, Apps, App management, FocusForce, Battery usage: allow background activity.
Turn on Auto launch (also called Startup manager) for FocusForce.
Allow Floating windows if the option is listed under permissions.
Open Recent apps and lock the FocusForce card.

string-array.name: oem_tips_vivo
string-array.item: Settings, Battery, Background power consumption management: set FocusForce to Allow high background power consumption.
i Manager, App manager, Autostart: turn on FocusForce.
Settings, Apps, Permissions: allow Display over other apps and Pop-ups while in background.
Open Recent apps and lock the FocusForce card.

string-array.name: oem_tips_samsung
string-array.item: Settings, Battery, Background usage limits: add FocusForce to Never sleeping apps and remove it from Sleeping or Deep sleeping apps.
Settings, Apps, FocusForce, Battery: choose Unrestricted.
Settings, Apps, FocusForce: turn off Pause app activity if unused.
Turn off Put unused apps to sleep in Battery settings.

string-array.name: oem_tips_realme
string-array.item: Settings, App management, App list, FocusForce, Battery usage: allow background activity.
Turn on Auto launch for FocusForce.
Allow Floating windows under permissions.
Open Recent apps and lock the FocusForce card.
